models_evaluated: SEPD (Sepsis on ED to PICU Disposition) model

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity in silent implementation versus model testing
links.effect: During silent implementation (1,058 encounters), the SEPD model maintained similar sensitivity (85.29%) and specificity (60.45%) to those observed during model testing.
links.quote: During silent implementation, the SEPD model maintained similar sensitivity (85.29%) and specificity (60.45%) to those observed during model testing.

links.outcome: Discrimination (AUROC) of the local model versus vendor-developed sepsis model
links.effect: SEPD model AUROC 81.8% compared to 57.5% for the vendor-developed sepsis model, with better precision-recall performance.
links.quote: The SEPD model outperformed a vendor-developed sepsis model with an AUROC of 81.8%, compared to 57.5%.

screen.reason: The study evaluates a pediatric sepsis predictive model during a prospective silent-mode deployment in an ED workflow and compares local model validation against an existing vendor model.

primary.practice: silent-mode deployment and local model validation against vendor model
